checks.title: No reverse polarity protection on a power input
Fast blow fuse where inrush is expected (bulk capacitance, motors, hot-plug): nuisance trips
Power outputs on connectors from nets used on board: suggest an eFuse or switch with short and overload protection
No overcurrent protection (fuse, polyfuse, eFuse) on a power input
No overvoltage protection (TVS, clamp, OVP switch) on a power input
No input filter (bulk capacitor, ferrite or LC) on a power input
Fuse rating vs the expected current: holds the worst-case normal load, blows on the fault it is there for
TVS standoff voltage below the input's operating maximum: it conducts in normal operation and burns
TVS clamping voltage above the absolute maximum of what it protects (the regulator or part behind it)
Polyfuse hold current below the load, or its resistance in series with a supply that needs to be accurate
Fuse or polyfuse rated above the connector, cable or trace it protects
Two power sources on one net (battery and USB, two inputs, two connectors) without ORing diodes, an ideal-diode controller or a switch
Reverse protection by a series diode on an input over about 1 A: suggest a PMOS ideal diode (dissipation, dropout)
No bulk capacitance where a supply arrives through a long cable or is hot-plugged: inductive overshoot on connection can exceed ratings
Fuse voltage rating below the supply voltage (32 V DC fuses on a 48 V input)
No undervoltage lockout on a power input whose source can sag (battery, long cable): regulators restart in a loop and loads see a brown-out
PMOS reverse-polarity switch with |Vin| above its Vgs(max) and no gate zener or divider, or a standard-threshold FET on an input of 5 V or less that never turns fully on ≈ DRV-10
Power input pins of parts not powered
DC-DC or LDO ref voltage known: find the divider, calculate output, compare with net name or specified voltage ≈ RAIL-3
Net name carries a voltage (e.g. `_3V3`) that is wrong
Fixed-output regulator whose MPN voltage differs from the net it feeds (a 3.3 V TLV70233 on `+1V8_LDO`) ≈ RAIL-2
Power net with loads but no source: no regulator output, connector, switch, ferrite or 0R from a sourced net (`+5V0_FLT` with nothing feeding it) ≈ RAIL-1
Current-limit resistor (ILIM, ISET, RLIM) vs the limit the design states: recompute from the datasheet formula
Feedback divider impedance outside the datasheet range: too high for the FB bias current and noise, too low for the quiescent budget
LDO output capacitor not what the part needs for stability: value below the minimum, ceramic on a part that needs ESR, or the other way round
LDO headroom below its dropout at load (3.3 V from a 3.6 V battery through a 0.5 V dropout part)
Switching regulator bootstrap (BST, BOOT) capacitor missing or far from the datasheet value
Feedback divider sensing the wrong node: before a ferrite, filter or switch, so the regulated voltage is not the one the load sees
Conversion ratio vs switching frequency: minimum on-time or maximum duty cycle violated (24 V to 1 V at 2 MHz, 3.3 V from 3.6 V on a buck without 100 % mode)
Boost converter output not isolated when disabled: the input reaches the output through the inductor and diode, so "off" is Vin
PGOOD / PG open-drain output without a pull-up, or pulled to a rail that is not up when it is read
Enable pin tied or driven above its maximum (EN rated 6 V tied to a 12 V Vin), or driven from a rail below its high threshold
Soft-start, compensation or timing pins (SS, COMP, RT, CT) without the parts the datasheet requires
Regulator configuration pins (MODE, SYNC, FREQ, FPWM, VSEL) floating where the datasheet says tie them
Two regulator outputs tied together without a part that allows it (parallel LDOs fight, one sinks)
Analog supply (VDDA, AVDD, VREF+) fed straight from the digital rail without a filter
Reference input (VREF+, REF, VREFIN) without its own decoupling, or sourced from a noisy rail
Total output capacitance of a regulator outside its stable range after ceramic DC-bias derating (a 10 µF 0603 at 5 V is about 4 µF), or more than its soft-start and current limit can charge
Inductor value outside the datasheet range for the switching frequency and current
Regulator symbol shared by orderable siblings with different VFB or Vout (0.6 / 0.8 V, 1.8 / 3.3 V): the divider or the net was computed for the other sibling, the MPN decides ≈ RAIL-2, RAIL-4
Regulator EN pin floating on a part without an internal pull: never starts, or starts at random
Input range below the regulator's minimum Vin or UVLO at the low end (a 4.5 V-minimum buck on a 3-cell battery) ≈ RATE-12
Asynchronous converter rectifying through a slow diode or a MOSFET body diode instead of a Schottky: losses and reverse recovery
No decoupling capacitors on power nets
Recommended decoupling values
STM32 VCAP pins need 2.2 µF ceramic caps
Caution against ferrite beads without measurements
Datasheet-specified filter or bypass capacitors (PLL, CRFILT, VCORE, VCAP, VDDA filter) missing or at a different value than the datasheet gives
Bulk capacitance on a rail below what its regulator or load needs (sum per rail, derated)
Fewer decoupling capacitors than power pins on a part that wants one per pin
Decoupling only on the source side of a ferrite, filter or series resistor: nothing at the pin it serves
Ferrite bead in series with a high-current rail: saturates, and its DC resistance drops the rail
Bypass capacitor on the IC's power pin but not on the rail: a two-pin net of one passive and one power pin passes every ERC and powers nothing
Parallel ceramics a decade apart (10 µF with 10 nF): anti-resonance between them; prefer multiples of one value or a graded set
Polarized capacitor (electrolytic, tantalum) with its negative terminal on the higher-potential net
Datasheet-specified bias or set resistors (RBIAS, ISET, RZQ, RREF, EXTRES) missing, off value, or looser than the tolerance asked (240 Ω 1 %, 4.87k 1 %) ≈ DEC-5
Power sequencing: intermittent problems on power on or off
Feedback or bootstrap loops, e.g. EN set by a divider powered by the device's own output, never starts
SD card insertion inrush: no power switch or resistor; decoupling after that switch or resistor ≈ SEQ-6
Soft start circuits with a MOSFET or resistor as load; if load is specified, report performance
High voltage net without self-discharge resistors

Power switch turning hard on into a capacitive load (a downstream board, a hot-plug port): the inrush dips the source and resets the board's own parts. Slow turn-on, fast turn-off (gate RC with a diode, or a load switch with soft start)
Multi-rail part (SoC, FPGA, DDR) whose datasheet orders its supplies, with nothing on the board enforcing the order
Reset of a multi-rail part released by an RC alone, not gated by its rails being valid: no supervisor or PGOOD chain
Output capacitors not discharged at power-off for a part that needs a full power-on reset: a quick off-on leaves it half powered
Split grounds without an isolated circuit: warn, point to books and pages
Suggest a Y cap between isolated grounds
Analog and digital grounds joined at more than one point, or not joined at all
Net crossing an isolation barrier: a label or power symbol of one side used on the other (`GND` on the isolated side)
Non-isolated part or structure spanning the barrier: a pull-up, capacitor, resistor or protection diode between the two sides, a debug header ground, a shield or a mounting hole bonded on both
Isolation rating of the isolators, transformers and Y capacitors vs the voltage the barrier must hold
Chassis or shield ground tied straight to signal ground, or left floating, without a decision (R, C, or direct) ≈ USB-4
MOSFET gate threshold vs driving level
High side MOSFETs driven incorrectly
PWM from MCU or SoC pins driving transistors directly: suggest a driver to protect the pin
Several gates on one driver: check charge pump capacity
MOSFET as inverter: gate resistor to stop Cgd pulling the output below ground
Q-Q chain not back to back, e.g. pogo-pin VBUS protection; double check thresholds
No snubbers on half bridge output
Flyback without feedback and no resistive or zener load on output
Relays without flyback diode
Gate drive beyond Vgs(max): a high-side PMOS on a 24 V rail with its gate pulled to ground sees −24 V on a ±20 V gate
MOSFET body diode conducting in the off state: source and drain swapped, or a load switch oriented so the load is fed through the diode
BJT base driven from a logic pin without a base resistor
Low-side switch under a load whose signals are ground-referenced elsewhere: the load's ground floats when off
Inductive load (solenoid, motor, coil, transformer) switched without a freewheel diode, TVS or snubber ≈ DRV-9
Half bridge driven by one signal and its inverter with no dead time: both transistors on during the edge
Gate driver bootstrap diode or capacitor missing
LED driven from a GPIO or a rail without a series resistor or current limit
LED forward voltage above its rail (a white or blue LED on 1.8 V, two in series on 3.3 V): never lights
No gate resistor between a gate driver and a MOSFET: ringing and EMI
Rds(on) only specified at a gate voltage above the drive available (a 10 V-rated FET driven at 3.3 V) ≈ DRV-1
Rechargeable lithium cell without protection (overvoltage, undervoltage, overcurrent), on the pack or the board
Charger thermistor pin (TS, NTC) floating or tied in a way that disables charging, instead of a thermistor or the documented fixed divider
Charger without power path while the system load sits on the battery: the load defeats termination and the cell never finishes charging
Primary cell (coin cell, alkaline) with a path that can charge it (a diode-less connection to a rail, a charger)
Battery connector polarity vs the common convention for that connector (JST PH packs, barrel jacks)
Regulator or boost running from a battery without undervoltage lockout: drains the cell to zero
Fuel gauge sense resistor not in the leg the gauge expects (low side vs high side)
Net shunting a known part (R, C, L, transistor...): most likely a net label collision, or a port and net label with the same name ≈ SHORT-2
Accidental net name collision, e.g. on I2C: VCCa-R-R-VCCa/b, or two 0R leading to the same net
Non-DNM part shunting another mounted part
Short circuit between power and ground through low value resistor(s)
VDD/VCC pins shorted to GND, or GND/VEE to power nets
Inputs shorted to ground or power without a resistor
Shorted IOs: warn that they must be driven together
Direct connections to battery and other high energy nets
Power to ground through a forward-biased diode or a MOSFET body diode
Power to ground through a TVS or zener whose standoff voltage is below the net voltage
Two push-pull outputs on one net (output-output conflict)
Differential pair with P tied to N: a label typo or a wrong bus entry
Net with a single pin (a label with no partner, a typo in one of two labels)
Net names that differ only in case, separator or suffix (`RESET_N` and `RESET_n`, `3V3` and `+3V3`): almost always one net meant
Label not attached to a wire or pin (dangling, offset by a grid step)
Hierarchical sheet pin without a matching label inside the sheet, or unconnected on the parent
Power symbol and a signal label with the same name: the signal is silently on the rail
Global label used on one sheet only, where a local label was meant (or the other end is misspelled)
No-connect flag on a pin that also has a wire
Unconnected pin without a no-connect flag: not decided, or forgotten
No-connect flag on a pin the datasheet says must be tied (an unused input, a mode pin, an exposed pad)
Hidden power pins on a symbol connected implicitly by name: the connection is not visible on the sheet
Unnamed (auto-named) net with many pins or crossing sheets: give it a name
Same label text in different scopes (a local and a global label, a sheet pin and a global label): joined in one tool, separate in another, and the designer assumes one of the two
Output pin whose net reaches no input (an output into nothing but passives or a test point)
Ground-named pin (GND, VSS, AGND, PGND) on a net that is not a ground
Four-way wire junction, or a label placed over several wires: the connection is ambiguous to a reader
Bus mismatch: a member net not in the bus it joins, bus widths that differ, indices out of range
ERC or DRC rules silenced in the project file: list them in the report, they hide findings
Power backfeed through IO, suggest Ioff capable buffers
General case: two power domains, IO across, one domain goes off, IO powers it through protection diodes ≈ BKF-1
Same through a MOSFET body diode, e.g. in an I2C voltage translator
Backfeed through MOSFETs, e.g. in DC-DC converters
Backfeed through LDOs
Backfeed through internal IC structure where known (beyond IO protection diodes)
Power through IO or I2C lines; also spots 1-Wire, can exclude
I2C device on a rail that can be off (backfeed should catch this)

Pins on a connector that an external device can drive while this board is unpowered: op-amp and MCU input clamps, pull-up PMOS body diodes and ESD diodes feed the rails. Needs powered-off-safe inputs, large series resistance or back-to-back switches
Level shifter or buffer whose own pull-ups feed an unpowered target through its outputs
USB VBUS joined to a system rail without a diode or switch on a board that can also be externally powered or act as host
Pull-up from a rail that can be off onto a bus that stays on: the bus feeds the off rail through the resistor and drags low ≈ BKF-7
Resistor divider straight on a power rail, draining power all the time
Pins that can't be high in some power states (go to another domain): list them even if the warning is suppressed
NC pins: suggest setting them to analog or pulling them to cut power draw
Resistor divider or pull through a normally closed button or switch: current flows in the rest state
Indicator LED permanently on a battery rail
Pull-up on a line that is held low in sleep (or pull-down on one held high): steady current in the low power state
Battery measurement divider always connected: suggest a switched divider or a high-side switch ≈ LEAK-1
Pull-up, divider or other circuitry to a different voltage level (needs IO bank voltage; easy for single supply parts)
1V8 output to 3V3 input and similar: compare thresholds
I2C thresholds may allow skipping a translator, e.g. 1V8 into a 3V3 device with Vth 1.4 V
I2C discrete translator pull-up to the wrong voltage
Bidirectional level shifter used for unidirectional signals (e.g. USART + boot mode)
A better suited bank exists for the net voltage or target bank voltage
Several power rails on a part and no banks defined: warn
Signal not referenced to GND, e.g. an inverting buck and its enable signal
Discrete translator (BSS138 pair) with a gate reference that gives the wrong threshold for one side
Higher-voltage output into a lower-voltage input above its absolute maximum (5 V into a 3.3 V pin that is not 5 V tolerant)

Edge-accelerated auto-direction shifter (TXS01xx class) driving push-pull signals into a pull-down, a long line or capacitance: the high is held only by its weak pull-up, so SWD, UART and SPI come out slow and low. Use a direction-controlled translator (2T45 class)
Level shifter direction pin (DIR) floating, or fixed against the signal's direction
Level shifter output enable floating, or enabled before both of its rails are up
Digital isolator or transceiver channel direction against the signal (TX into an input channel)
Single-MOSFET open-drain shifter (BSS138 pair) on a fast push-pull line (SPI over a few MHz, WS2812 data): too slow, use a buffer or a direction-controlled translator
Input pin without a drive source, smart about resistors, FETs etc. ≈ IO-2
IO to an input without pull-up/down: High-Z gives an undefined state
Enable driven by an MCU or SoC GPIO without a pull: think of uninit and reboot state; `default_gpio_state` part property overrides
Assume IO pins are high/low/Z by default and look for bugs ≈ IO-5
If IO pin default states are known, derive checks
High impedance nets acting as touch buttons ≈ IO-1
Button to ground with a pull-down, or button to power with a pull-up ≈ IO-8
Mention a needed pull-up or down where it applies, e.g. buttons

Pins a part drives in its non-firmware modes: ROM bootloader, factory test, reset and fault states. A ROM bootloader configures its interfaces (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN, USB) and may drive or toggle those pins while it scans for a host, with no firmware to keep anything else safe; check what each such pin controls (switches, enables, buses, resets) and what that level does there. Example: an STM32 ROM bootloader drives its USART TX pin high while it scans for a host; if that pin also selects a USB data switch, a firmware update over the ROM cuts the downstream device's data ≈ IO-3, IO-4
Input driven only from a connector: floats when nothing is plugged in ≈ IO-6
MOSFET gate without a pull: floats while its driver is in reset or unpowered
Output enable (`~OE`, `~G`, `EN`) of a shift register, driver, mux or buffer without a pull to its disabled state: outputs do whatever until firmware loads them

Peripheral reset pin pulled into reset by default, driven by a controller that resets: every controller reset (also into its ROM bootloader) takes the peripheral down with it. Decide on purpose: a pull-up with the controller able to drive low keeps the peripheral configured ≈ LOGIC-5
Configuration, mode or address straps of a non-MCU part (PHY, hub, codec, sensor) floating where the datasheet requires a level
Open-drain interrupt or fault output without a pull-up
Pull-up and pull-down both on one net: an accidental divider, neither level clean
Pull value too weak for the leakage on the net (1 MΩ against ESD diode and input leakage) or too strong for the driver (1 kΩ on an open-drain output)
Button without a debounce capacitor where the firmware assumes an RC filter
Logical contradictions in GPIO or GPIO expander connections · AI prompt: check that GPIOs that drive multiple things have no logical contradictions, table of each occurrence
IO going to two MCUs or SoCs: odd requirements likely, esp. IRQs and buttons not going to reset inputs
Suggest buffering high fan-out signals
Total IO current per IC or bank

Dependency loops in bring-up, update or recovery: part A only works once part B has set it up, while B needs A to start, update or recover. Then the board works while the firmware runs and fails exactly when it is needed (dead or half-written firmware, reset, ROM bootloader). Walk every boot, update and recovery path with each programmable part in its reset or unconfigured state. Example: an MCU whose only update path (its USB ROM bootloader) goes through a USB hub that the MCU itself must release from reset and configure over I2C: after a reset the bootloader never reaches the host. Same shape elsewhere: a sequencer or supervisor powered or configured by what it controls, a clock or PHY configured by the chip it serves, a config memory written through the bus it configures, a mux or level shifter on the programming path driven by the target ≈ SEQ-2
Current through one pin above its maximum (an LED without resistor, a relay coil, a long pull chain) ≈ LOGIC-4
Open-drain or open-collector output as the only driver of a net with no pull-up: never goes high
Polarity mismatch by name: an active-low output (`_N`, `#`, `~`) into an active-high input or the reverse (`PGOOD` into `~EN`, `INT_N` into a rising-edge IRQ) with no inverter
SCL goes to a pin named SCL, MISO to MISO etc
MCUs with SVD/pin data: check the alternate function actually supports the mode used
SLG* (GreenPAK): suggest using all pins, e.g. to monitor things, connect to ENs, route EN through if inverting or delay is needed
GPIO on a pin that is NRST, BOOT or another reset-time function by default (STM32G0 PF2-NRST, option-byte controlled): the firmware never gets the pin, or a low resets the chip
Debug pins (SWDIO, SWCLK, JTAG) reused as GPIO: debugging and flashing lost once the firmware runs ≈ DBG-1
Analog signal (ADC, DAC, comparator) on a pin without that analog function
One peripheral signal on two pins, or two uses of a shared peripheral (USB and CAN on an STM32F103 share one SRAM block)
5 V net on a pin that is not 5 V tolerant where the part has tolerant (FT) pins to choose from ≈ LVL-10
Boot or strapping pin with no defined level at reset (no pull, no driver that is up at that moment)

Strapping pin shared with a signal that another device may drive at reset: a UART bridge on ESP32 GPIO0, a card or display on an i.MX boot config pin, a PHY LED with a pull that changes its mode strap
Strapping pin pulled to a mode the design does not want (STM32 BOOT0 high boots the ROM, ESP32 GPIO12 high selects 1.8 V flash)
Boot pin wired but ignored by the factory option bytes or fuses (STM32G0 nBOOT_SEL): a programming step must enable it, say so in the bring-up notes
No way to force the ROM bootloader (button, jumper, header pin) on a board updated in the field
ROM bootloader interface not reachable from outside with the firmware dead: behind a hub, mux or shifter that only firmware configures ≈ LOGIC-5
Boot memory on pins or a bus the ROM cannot boot from (QSPI flash on a non-boot CS, SD on a non-boot SDIO instance), or a flash whose command set the ROM's loader does not support
Part strapped for a configuration that assumes a controller (a hub strapped for SMBus config powers up with every register at zero): fine only if that controller is always there first
Strapping pin shared with a peripheral signal without a series resistor between them: the peripheral loads the strap during the latch window, the strap must win
FPGA configuration pins (mode select MSEL/CFG, nCONFIG/PROGRAM_B, nSTATUS/INIT_B, CONF_DONE/DONE, PUDC_B, nCE/nCEO) floating or without the pull-ups and pull-downs the configuration guide requires
MCU with CAN or USB and no crystal
HS crystal capacitors should be high frequency rated
Crystal NC pins may need to go to ground
Crystal pins used as IO: warn about low drive strength
No pull-up on a reset_n input
Suggest a cap on buttons to reset inputs; note hw debounce in the programmer report
No capacitor on a reset_n input: noise and brown-outs reach it ≈ CLK-6
Crystal load capacitors vs the crystal's CL: C1 = C2 ≈ 2·CL − Cstray; far off means the frequency is off or it does not start
Crystal ESR and drive level vs the oscillator: gain margin (gm / gm_crit) under 5, or no series resistor where the drive level is exceeded (ST AN2867)
Crystal frequency outside the range the part's oscillator supports
32.768 kHz crystal with a CL or ESR the low-power oscillator cannot drive
Active oscillator output into a crystal pin without bypass mode or the attenuation the datasheet asks for
Oscillator or clock buffer output-enable / standby pin floating
Reset input driven by a push-pull output: fights the debugger, supervisor or button that also drives it; reset lines are open-drain
One reset net shared by the MCU and its peripherals: a debugger reset (or a watchdog) resets the whole board, and peripherals lose configuration on every firmware restart ≈ IO-13
RTC in use with VBAT floating, no backup source, or no 32 kHz crystal
External watchdog with no way to disable it for debugging (jumper, DNM resistor)
Clock output fanned out to several loads without a buffer or series termination
Crystal tolerance vs the interface that uses it: USB HS ±500 ppm, Ethernet ±50 ppm, BLE ±50 ppm or tighter, CAN FD per bit rate
No pull-ups on an I2C bus
I2C multiple pull-ups
Pull-up from two series resistors to nowhere (part of I2C-1)
Pull-up to a non-rail net (resistor with only two pins connected)?
I2C address collision (needs addresses in the library, maybe AI can pull them out)
I2C going to a connector that isn't FPC or fine pitch B2B: suggest another interface, keep I2C on board?
Series tie resistor on an I2C line too high (over 100 Ω)

Pull-up too weak for the bus speed: Rp > tr_max / (0.847 · Cb), tr (30-70 %) max 1000 ns at 100k, 300 ns at 400k, 120 ns at 1M; Cb estimated from the pins on the net (or a project setting). Measured on a bench: ~135 pF per line, 10k gives 1170 ns (fails 100k), 2.2k 277 ns (meets 400k), 1M needs ≤ 1.05k
Pull-up value outside the recommended range (2.2k-10k): too strong for the sink current (3 mA, 20 mA in Fm+), too weak for the edges ≈ I2C-8
SCL and SDA pull-ups of different value
I2C device whose supply can be off while the bus is on, without fail-safe (Ioff) inputs: it feeds itself through its ESD diodes and clamps both lines to ~0.6 V, the whole bus is dead ≈ BKF-8

SMBus device on an I2C bus: it times out when the clock drops under 10 kHz or a transfer stalls over 25-35 ms, and its fixed thresholds (0.8 / 2.1 V in SMBus 2.0, 0.8 / 1.35 V in 3.0) do not match I2C's 0.3 / 0.7 VDD on 5 V and 1.8 V buses
Static-offset bus buffers (P82B96, PCA9600, PCA9515 class) in series, or one facing a device with a low VIL: the buffer's ~0.5 V low is never seen as low, the bus locks

Push-pull auto-direction shifter (TXB010x class) on I2C: its direction sensing fails on open-drain lines and with pull-ups under ~50k. Edge-accelerated open-drain parts (TXS01xx) work but their one-shots can glitch slow edges; a plain open-drain shifter (PCA9306, BSS138 pair) is the safe choice ≈ LVL-11
I2C mux or switch whose channels, joined by firmware, carry devices with the same address, or whose summed capacitance exceeds the limit
Device at a reserved address: 0x00-0x07 (general call, CBUS, Hs master codes) or 0x78-0x7F (10-bit prefix, device ID)
Address straps (A0-A2, ADDR, SA0) floating: the address is undefined, or read at power-up only
Bus segment behind a translator, isolator, buffer or mux with no pull-ups of its own ≈ I2C-1
Pull-ups of a segment to a rail that can be off while the rest of the bus is on ≈ BKF-12
Device that stretches the clock for its conversions on a master known not to support stretching (BCM2835 and its errata)
Estimated bus capacitance over 400 pF (long cable, many devices): needs a buffer or a slower mode ≈ I2C-8
Several masters on one bus: all controllers must support multi-master arbitration, and the firmware must handle bus-busy
USART TX connected to TX (not crossed)
SPI CS line grounded: some ICs need it to work
CAN terminator based on MOSFETs or SSRs
LVDS without terminators
Not the whole bus is present, maybe nets shorted out ≈ SER-6
Not the whole bus is connected to a device
CAN TX and RX crossed between MCU and transceiver (they are not crossed, unlike UART)
UART flow control mis-paired: CTS to CTS, or RTS of one side not to CTS of the other
RS-485 bus without termination at both ends (120 Ω) where this board is an end node
RS-485 without fail-safe biasing (A pulled up, B pulled down) on a transceiver without built-in fail-safe: idle bus reads noise
RS-485 DE / ~RE without a pull to the receive state: the transceiver may drive the bus while the MCU is in reset
RS-485 A/B or CAN H/L swapped against the connector's documented pinout
CAN termination wrong for the node's place: none at a bus end, or a 120 Ω on a node in the middle
CAN split termination (2 × 60 Ω) without the centre capacitor to ground
CAN transceiver STB, S or EN pin floating: it stays in standby or silent mode
CAN FD data rate above the transceiver's class (a classic 1 Mbit/s transceiver on a 5 Mbit/s FD bus)
Transceiver logic side (VIO) on a different rail than the MCU pins it talks to
SPI chip select shared by two slaves, or a slave whose MISO does not tri-state when deselected on a shared MISO
SPI slave CS without a pull-up (flash, sensor, any slave): floats during the host's reset, the slave sees commands in the noise and a second slave answers on a shared MISO
RS-232 levels (±12 V) straight into MCU pins, no transceiver
USB-UART bridge RTS / DTR wired to boot and reset for auto-programming, or deliberately not: say which
1-Wire with parasitically powered devices and only a weak pull-up: suggest a strong pull-up switch

RS-485 or CAN node with no ground reference to the bus (no ground wire, no isolation), or its ground tied straight to the remote ground (loop): the standards want a resistor-separated ground or an isolated node
RS-485 unit-load budget exceeded: nodes plus the bias network over 32 UL (256 with 1/8-UL transceivers)

Magnetics centre taps terminated for the wrong PHY type (current-mode PHYs want the taps tied to the supply, voltage-mode PHYs want separate taps to ground through capacitors; DP83848C §7.2, KSZ9031 §12), or only two of the four taps terminated on a gigabit design copied from 10/100
RGMII delay: neither the PHY's internal delay strap nor the MAC provides the 2 ns skew, or both do
MDIO without a pull-up (1.5k-10k)
PHY address straps unset, two PHYs on one MDIO bus with the same address, or address 0 on a PHY that treats it as broadcast
Unused pairs and centre taps without Bob Smith termination (75 Ω to a 1 nF 2 kV capacitor to chassis), or with it returned to signal ground, on the PHY side, or through a cap below 2 kV
RMII REF_CLK direction wrong: both or neither side sources the 50 MHz
PHY LED pins that double as configuration straps: the LED and its pull set a mode at reset
MDI pair polarity or pair order against the jack's pinout (Auto-MDIX saves pair swaps, not always polarity)
PHY crystal tolerance above ±50 ppm
PoE powered device without isolation of the PD side, or without the classification resistor
RGMII / RMII lines without the series resistors the PHY's reference design uses
PHY reset released before its clock is stable, or with no pull at all
Magnetics not rated for the design: isolation under 1500 Vac, or not PoE-rated where PoE current biases the core
PHY multi-level strap divider computed without the pin's internal pull (9k-40k, ±25 %), with 5 % resistors, or with a capacitor straight on the strap
SD / eMMC CMD and DAT lines without pull-ups (10k-100k)
DDR pin swap across bytes and other errors
SD / eMMC CLK with a pull-up, or CD / WP switch pins without one
SPI / QSPI flash WP#, HOLD# or RESET# floating: writes blocked or the part held at random
SD card detect wired to the wrong pins (shell instead of the switch pins, or to ground on a socket that signals to VDD)
eMMC VCCQ on a different voltage than the host's IO bank, or RST_n without a pull-up
